The representative hot tank was modeled using SS 347H, with thermal expansion coefficient of 1.89x10- 5 K-1 and Poisson ratio of 0.31 [7], and its temperature-dependent mechanical properties, i.e. Young’s modulus (YM), yield strength (YS), and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) referenced in the Appendix A, Figure A1. The structural analysis established specific boundary conditions for the tank floor; the bottom edge was set as a fixed support, while the rest of the floor was treated as an elastic support with a stiffness of 0.015 N mm-3 [8]. The friction coefficient between the floor and the sand foundation was set to 0.5 and the 10,800 kg weight of the sparger ring was evenly distributed across its eight supports. Additional thermophysical properties for the salt, air, and tank components are presented in Tables A1 to A3 in the Appendix A [9-14]. Figure 4. Schematic diagram of the hot tank model. The developed hot tank model was then used to evaluate the distribution and evolution of temperature, stress, and deformation in the tank under typical operation conditions. For the specific analyses of tank size and preheating, the model assessed the impact of tank diameter, floor thickness, and a typical preheating process on the stress and deformation in the tank floor. 1.4 Lessons Learned from Task 1-5 This report presents the results and analysis for Task 6 (Impact of Tank Size) and Task 7 (Tank Preheating Process) conducted under the project agreement DE-EE0038475. The results and analysis for Tasks 1 to 5 for this project were presented in the report NREL/TP-5700-89036 published in March 2024 [4]. Some of the main lessons learned from Tasks 1 to 5 are summarized as follows: - Failures in molten salt tanks – The integrity of molten salt TES tanks in CSP plants is compromised by mechanisms such as stress relaxation cracking, buckling, low-cycle fatigue, and creep, all influenced by design, material quality, and operating conditions. The results isolate creep as the primary driver of failure, predicting that combined stresses will cause tank floor failure after few years of operation. - Tank design – Tanks are usually designed following guidelines from API 650 and ASME BPVC Section II standards.
